title: Close Separable C*-Algebras Without Spatial Conjugacy
main_claim: For every eps>0 there are unital norm-separable C*-algebras A,B on a separable H with a common identity, d_KK(A,B)<eps and A''=B'', such that no unitary conjugates A onto B. The construction is A=E_D(P_0), B=E_D(P_t): sequences in D that converge to an element of P. Here P_a=C*(lambda(g) tensor pi_a(g)) with pi_t a Pytlik-Szwarc-type deformation of lambda on F_infinity.
coverage:
I checked every step line by line.
- Prop 2.1: closedness and separability; equality d_KK(E_D(P),E_D(Q))=d_KK(P,Q) in both directions; the center equals the convergent scalar sequences, so the e_n are exactly the minimal central projections; a conjugating unitary permutes the e_n; the corners equal D, so each U_n normalizes D; pulling back constant sequences gives U_n^* b U_n -> p_b; the two algebras have the same commutant.
- Lem 2.3: the identity is invariant under conjugation by unitaries normalizing D, using conjugation by U tensor U, and it survives the limit.
- Cor 2.4: the distance bound 2||W-I||.
- Lem 3.1: the Gram matrix of the xi vectors is t^{d(x,y)}, so pi_t is a well-defined unitary representation. T=pi_t(g)lambda(g)* fixes every delta_y off the geodesic [e,g], because the first steps toward e and toward g coincide there. On the path, T=XR'-tS with X=R(I-tS*)^{-1}. Numerically (python), T restricted to the path span is unitary and ||T-I|| is about 2t, below c(t), for path lengths up to 80 and t in {0.05,0.1,0.3,0.6}.
- Lem 4.1: the absorption identity.
- Lem 4.2: D' = lambda(G)' tensor 1, and D has scalar center because F_infinity is ICC and Y lies in L(G) intersect R(G); W=W_{pi_t}W_{lambda}^* gives ||W-I|| = sup_x ||pi_t(x)-lambda(x)||.
- Lem 4.3: V conjugates P_0 onto 1 tensor C*_lambda(G) and commutes with D'.
- Lem 4.4: ||sum lambda(s_i)|| <= 2 sqrt(m) via the A_i/B_i splitting.
- Lem 4.5: the vector state gives a lower bound of mt for the product norm; absorption with sigma = pi_t tensor rho tensor 1 bounds the tensor norm by 2 sqrt(m).
- Final assembly.
I did not check the cited BOT13 and PS86, but the proof does not depend on them; the paper proves the deformation estimate directly.
sibling_notes: Rank 330 (Universal strong Kadison-Kastler stability) is in the same family but concerns von Neumann algebras / II_1 factors. This paper says explicitly that it gives no von Neumann counterexample (here A''=B''), so the two do not conflict and share no lemmas. This paper is self-contained and short. Since it settles a long-standing open problem, an expert should still recheck it, but I found no failing step.
